design_choice_and_rationale.chosen_mechanism: Reuses the summary_index / summary_rev mechanism merged in REGISTRY-SUMMARY-PAGE-NO-RESCAN-20261127 instead of introducing a second cache design: stored column lineage_index JSONB on registry.entries (holding the 14 pre-projected flat lineage fields for every object entry row) shares the existing summary_rev BIGINT column, sequence pantheon_registry_summary_rev_seq, and BEFORE INSERT OR UPDATE OF payload trigger entries_strategy_summary_index_tg (pantheon_registry_summary_index_tg_fn calling pantheon_registry_summary_index_build and pantheon_registry_lineage_index_build), plus partial index entries_lineage_index_idx (ON registry.entries (summary_rev ASC) WHERE lineage_index IS NOT NULL) and idempotent bounded batched backfill at store bootstrap (LINEAGE_INDEX_BACKFILL_BATCH_SIZE = 1000, FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED, leaving updated_at unchanged), paired with a single-flight in-process stamp-validated compiled adjacency cache (_CompiledLineageRowList / _CompiledLineageGraphIndex, bounded to LINEAGE_INDEX_MAX_TENANT_VIEWS = 16 tenant views) validated on every read by one cheap aggregate query (SELECT count(*), coalesce(max(summary_rev), 0)::bigint, coalesce(sum(summary_rev), 0)::bigint FROM registry.entries WHERE lineage_index IS NOT NULL) and updated incrementally in O(degree) time after writes via partial index entries_lineage_index_idx (WHERE lineage_index IS NOT NULL AND summary_rev > %s).
why_both_stored_columns_and_incremental_: 1. Eliminates per-request full-table payload detoasting and 14 JSON path evaluations in PostgreSQL: storing the pre-projected ~410.4-byte lineage_index JSONB and shared 8-byte summary_rev BIGINT on registry.entries drops Postgres lineage read buffer hits on 9,944 hosted-shape rows (9,418 strategy_spec, 344 execution_bundle, 182 alpha_template) from 114,607 shared buffers / 712.06 ms down to 2,881 shared buffers / 59.48 ms on a cold stored-column scan, 2,881 shared buffers / 4.81 ms on a warm stamp query, and 6 shared buffers / 0.101 ms on a post-write 1-row delta index scan.

2. Eliminates per-request full-population Python JSON decoding and adjacency graph reconstruction: across 8 concurrent cold reads on a fresh process, single-flight stamp-validated compiled adjacency (_CompiledLineageGraphIndex) collapses 8 reads to 1 SQL load + 1 adjacency build + 7 cache hits, cutting wall time from 11,509.03-22,332.28 ms to 2,007.74-3,809.58 ms (vs 16,244.52-28,424.18 ms for uncached stored-column reads) and peak RSS (VmHWM) from 460.61-541.42 MiB (+371.24-452.08 MiB delta) to 216.19-216.71 MiB (+126.81-127.33 MiB delta, well within DEV_MEM_LIMIT_REGISTRY=768m). Subsequent warm reads complete in 21.71-25.01 ms.

3. Immediate write visibility and single unified cache invalidation design: every write path atomically advances summary_rev and updates both summary_index and lineage_index in the same BEFORE trigger; the next read detects the stamp change, fetches only modified rows via summary_rev > prev_max_rev, and splices old/new edges incrementally in _CompiledLineageGraphIndex.apply_delta_rows.

runtime_budget.cap: 1 lineage_index JSONB (~410 B) and 1 shared summary_rev BIGINT (8 B) per object row in registry.entries; bootstrap backfill bounded by LINEAGE_INDEX_BACKFILL_BATCH_SIZE = 1000 and LINEAGE_INDEX_BACKFILL_MAX_BATCHES = 50; in-process lineage tenant view + adjacency cache bounded to LINEAGE_INDEX_MAX_TENANT_VIEWS = 16 with FIFO eviction
runtime_budget.cleanup: stored columns and partial index tuples follow registry.entries row lifecycle with PostgreSQL VACUUM; non-object rows set lineage_index = NULL via trigger; in-process cache evicts oldest tenant view beyond LINEAGE_INDEX_MAX_TENANT_VIEWS = 16, updates existing adjacency views incrementally on stamp change or evicts stale views on delete/retire, and supports full eviction via invalidate_lineage_index_cache(full=True)

rollback_compatibility.mechanism: lineage_index and summary_rev are nullable columns maintained by BEFORE INSERT OR UPDATE OF payload trigger entries_strategy_summary_index_tg; during a rollback, the previous release's INSERT/UPDATE/SELECT statements continue to succeed. If a rollback to the previous release replaces pantheon_registry_summary_index_tg_fn with the summary-only trigger (leaving lineage_index stale or summary_rev NULL on rows written during the rollback window), roll-forward bootstrap restores the shared trigger and backfill_lineage_index re-backfills any row where lineage_index IS NULL OR summary_rev IS NULL OR lineage_index IS DISTINCT FROM pantheon_registry_lineage_index_build(payload), bumping summary_rev via nextval whenever summary_rev was NULL or an existing lineage_index was stale.
